blocks.text: Yeh Unit 9 (Inverse Trigonometric (TOC: 'Inverse Trigonometric Functions and Their Graphs')) ke poore unit se practice short questions (mukhtasar sawal) hain, unit ke sections ki tarteeb mein, Board ke 2 number wale sawal ke andaz mein. Har sawal mukhtasar qadmon mein hal kiya gaya hai.
9.1 Inverse Trigonometric Functions and their Graph

blocks.prompt:
1 When does a function \(f : X \to Y\) have an inverse? How are the domain and range of \(f^{-1}\) related to those of \(f\)?
(Function \(f : X \to Y\) ka inverse kab hota hai? \(f^{-1}\) ki domain aur range ka \(f\) se kya rishta hai?)
blocks.explanation: Sirf jab \(f\) one-to-one aur onto (bijective) ho. Phir \(f^{-1} : Y \to X\); \(f^{-1}\) ki domain = \(f\) ki range, aur \(f^{-1}\) ki range = \(f\) ki domain; \(f^{-1}(y) = x\) jab \(f(x) = y\).

book_ref.quote: only a one-to-one and onto function will have an inverse

blocks.prompt:
2 Why do the trigonometric functions have no inverses on their whole domains? How is this put right?
(Trigonometric functions ke apni poori domain par inverse kyun nahin hote? Is ka hal kya hai?)
blocks.explanation: Yeh periodic hain, is liye bohat se angles aik hi value dete hain (maslan \(\sin\frac{\pi}{4} = \sin\frac{3\pi}{4}\)); one-to-one nahin. Domain ko aise interval tak mehdood karte hain jahan har value aik dafa aaye, aur codomain values ka set (maslan \([-1, 1]\)) lete hain; function bijective ho kar inverse rakhta hai.

book_ref.quote: by carefully restricting their domains and codomains, we can make these functions bijective

blocks.prompt:
3 Write \(\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}\) in inverse form and state how it is read.
(\(\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}\) ko inverse shakal mein likhein aur batayein kaise parhte hain.)
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{2\pi}{3} = \cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\) (kyunke \(y = \cos^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \cos y\), aur \(\frac{2\pi}{3} \in [0, \pi]\)). Parhein: '\(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) barabar hai cosine inverse of \(-\frac{1}{2}\)'.

book_ref.quote: Similarly, we can write the other equations as

blocks.prompt:
4 What is meant by the principal value of \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2}\)? Why is \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) not its value?
(\(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{2}\) ki principal value se kya muraad hai? \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) is ki value kyun nahin?)
blocks.explanation: Bohat se angles ka sine \(\frac{1}{2}\) hai. Principal value standard interval \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) wala aik angle hai: \(\frac{\pi}{6}\). \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\) is interval se bahar hai.

book_ref.quote: The single angle chosen in this way is called the principal value.

blocks.prompt:
5 Define the principal sine function and the inverse sine function. Give the domain and range of the inverse sine function.
(Principal sine function aur inverse sine function ki definition likhein. Inverse sine ki domain aur range batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Principal sine function: \(\sin : \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right] \to [-1, 1]\) (bijective). Inverse sine: \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \sin y\); domain \([-1, 1]\), range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\).

book_ref.quote: is called the principal sine function

blocks.prompt:
6 Find the principal values of \(\sin^{-1}(-1)\) and \(\sin^{-1} 0\).
(\(\sin^{-1}(-1)\) aur \(\sin^{-1} 0\) ki principal values nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: This is the test for every answer

blocks.prompt:
7 Evaluate \(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)\).
(\(\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)\) ki qeemat nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin\frac{3\pi}{4} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), is liye jawab \(\sin^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\pi}{4}\) (\(\frac{3\pi}{4}\) nahin, woh range se bahar hai).

book_ref.quote: must lie between \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\frac{\pi}{2}\)

blocks.prompt:
8 Does \(\sin^{-1}\frac{\pi}{2}\) exist? Give a reason.
(Kya \(\sin^{-1}\frac{\pi}{2}\) mojood hai? Wajah batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Nahin. \(\frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.571 > 1\), aur \(\sin^{-1}\) ki domain \([-1, 1]\) hai; kisi angle ka sine \(1\) se bara nahin hota. (\(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\) se mukhtalif hai.)

book_ref.quote: does not exist, because no angle has sine 2

blocks.prompt:
9 The point \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}, -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\) lies on the principal sine graph. Write the matching point on \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) and the line in which the two graphs are mirror images.
(Point \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}, -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\) principal sine graph par hai. \(y = \sin^{-1} x\) par mutabiq point aur woh line likhein jis mein dono graphs aik doosre ka aks hain.)
blocks.explanation: Coordinates badal jate hain: \(\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, -\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\), kyunke \(\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{3}\). Dono graphs line \(y = x\) mein aks hain.

book_ref.quote: Every point \((a, b)\) of \(y = \sin x\) gives the point \((b, a)\) of \(y = \sin^{-1} x\)

blocks.prompt:
10 Name two intervals, other than \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), on which the sine function is one-to-one with range \([-1, 1]\).
(\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) ke ilawa do intervals batayein jin par sine one-to-one ho aur range \([-1, 1]\) ho.)
blocks.explanation: Koi bhi \(\left[n\pi - \frac{\pi}{2}, n\pi + \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\): maslan \(\left[\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right]\) (\(n = 1\)) aur \(\left[-\frac{3\pi}{2}, -\frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) (\(n = -1\)).

book_ref.quote: where it is strictly increasing or decreasing, to make the sine function one-to-one

blocks.prompt:
11 Define the principal cosine function and the inverse cosine function, with domain and range.
(Principal cosine function aur inverse cosine function ki definition domain aur range ke saath likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Principal cosine function: \(\cos : [0, \pi] \to [-1, 1]\) (bijective). Inverse cosine: \(y = \cos^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \cos y\); domain \([-1, 1]\), range \([0, \pi]\).

book_ref.quote: is called the principal cosine function

blocks.prompt:
12 Why is the cosine function restricted to \([0, \pi]\) and not to \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)?
(Cosine ko \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) ke bajaye \([0, \pi]\) tak kyun mehdood karte hain?)
blocks.explanation: Cosine even hai: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\), is liye \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) par one-to-one nahin, aur wahan manfi bhi nahin hota. \([0, \pi]\) par yeh \(1\) se \(-1\) tak har value aik dafa leta hai.

book_ref.quote: Why not use \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) again, as for sine?

blocks.prompt:
13 Evaluate \(\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)\).
(\(\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right)\) ki qeemat nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\), is liye jawab \(\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \frac{\pi}{3}\) (\(-\frac{\pi}{3}\) range se bahar hai).

book_ref.quote: Cosine is an even function, so a negative angle and the matching positive angle always give the same value.

blocks.prompt:
14 Evaluate \(\cos^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\).
(\(\cos^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\) ki qeemat nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin\frac{7\pi}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\). \([0, \pi]\) mein cosine \(-\frac{1}{2}\) wala angle \(\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) hai.

book_ref.quote: Look at the negative inputs in the table: they give obtuse angles.

blocks.prompt:
15 Which is larger, \(\cos^{-1}(0.2)\) or \(\cos^{-1}(0.7)\)? Give a reason without a calculator.
(\(\cos^{-1}(0.2)\) aur \(\cos^{-1}(0.7)\) mein kaun bara hai? Calculator ke baghair wajah dein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos^{-1}(0.2)\). \(\cos^{-1} x\) decreasing (ghatne wala) function hai, is liye chhote number \(0.2\) ka angle bara hai.

book_ref.quote: A larger number has a smaller angle.

blocks.prompt:
16 Write the domain and range of \(f(x) = \tan x\), and explain why some points are left out of the domain.
(\(f(x) = \tan x\) ki domain aur range likhein, aur batayein ke kuch points domain se kyun nikaale gaye.)
blocks.explanation: Domain: \(\left\{x \mid x \in \mathbb{R},\ x \ne (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\right\}\); range: \(\mathbb{R}\). \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke odd multiples par \(\cos x = 0\); wahan sifar se taqseem hoti.

book_ref.quote: Division by zero is not defined, so these points are not in the domain.

blocks.prompt:
17 Define the principal tangent function and the inverse tangent function, with domain and range.
(Principal tangent function aur inverse tangent function ki definition domain aur range ke saath likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Principal tangent function: \(\tan : \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \to \mathbb{R}\) (bijective). Inverse tangent: \(y = \tan^{-1} x\) iff \(x = \tan y\); domain \((-\infty, \infty)\), range \(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\).

book_ref.quote: is called the principal tangent function

blocks.prompt:
18 Find the principal value of \(\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\).
(\(\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\) ki principal value nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\sqrt{3}\). Manfi value ka jawab manfi angle: \(\tan^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = -\frac{\pi}{3}\).

book_ref.quote: Use the sign and the principal range to place the angle

blocks.prompt:
19 Why is the range of \(\tan^{-1} x\) an open interval, while the range of \(\sin^{-1} x\) is closed?
(\(\tan^{-1} x\) ki range khula (open) interval kyun hai jab ke \(\sin^{-1} x\) ki band (closed)?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan\left(\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\) undefined hai, is liye \(\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\) values nahin ho saktin. Lekin \(\sin\left(\pm\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \pm 1\) mojood hain, is liye \(\sin^{-1}\) ki range band hai.

book_ref.quote: Why an open interval this time (round brackets)?

blocks.prompt:
20 Write the asymptotes of the graphs of the principal \(y = \tan x\) and of \(y = \tan^{-1} x\).
(Principal \(y = \tan x\) aur \(y = \tan^{-1} x\) ke graphs ke asymptotes likhein.)
blocks.explanation: Principal \(y = \tan x\): vertical asymptotes \(x = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\). \(y = \tan^{-1} x\): horizontal asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\) (\(y = x\) mein aks coordinates badal deta hai).

book_ref.quote: the coordinates swap, so vertical lines turn into horizontal lines

blocks.prompt:
21 Write the domain and range of \(f(x) = \csc x\) and explain the range.
(\(f(x) = \csc x\) ki domain aur range likhein aur range ki wajah batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Domain: \(x \ne n\pi\) (jahan \(\sin x \ne 0\)). Range: \((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\), kyunke \(|\sin x| \le 1\) se \(|\csc x| \ge 1\).

book_ref.quote: the reciprocal always has size at least 1

blocks.prompt:
22 Define the principal cosecant function and give the domain and range of the inverse cosecant function.
(Principal cosecant function ki definition likhein aur inverse cosecant ki domain aur range batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Principal cosecant: \(\csc : \left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right] \to (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\). \(y = \csc^{-1} x \iff x = \csc y\); domain \(\mathbb{R} - (-1, 1)\), range \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\).

book_ref.quote: called principal cosecant function

blocks.prompt:
23 Find the principal value of \(\csc^{-1}\left(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\).
(\(\csc^{-1}\left(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\) ki principal value nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\csc y = -\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\) yaani \(\sin y = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\); principal range mein \(y = -\frac{\pi}{3}\).

book_ref.quote: A quick example of our own. Find

blocks.prompt:
24 Why is \(0\) not in the range of \(\csc^{-1} x\)?
(\(0\) \(\csc^{-1} x\) ki range mein kyun nahin?)
blocks.explanation: \(\csc^{-1} x = 0\) ka matlab \(x = \csc 0 = \frac{1}{\sin 0}\), jo undefined hai. Is liye \(0\) nikaal diya; graph par \(y = 0\) horizontal asymptote hai.

book_ref.quote: That is why 0 is not in the range.

blocks.prompt:
25 Define the principal secant function and give the domain and range of the inverse secant function.
(Principal secant function ki definition likhein aur inverse secant ki domain aur range batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Principal secant: \(\sec : \left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right] \to (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\). \(y = \sec^{-1} x \iff x = \sec y\); domain \(\mathbb{R} - (-1, 1)\), range \(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\).

book_ref.quote: is called principal secant function
negative angles are outside the range of

blocks.prompt:
27 Write the range of \(\sec^{-1} x\) and explain why \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) is not in it.
(\(\sec^{-1} x\) ki range likhein aur batayein \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) is mein kyun nahin.)
blocks.explanation: Range: \(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\). \(\sec\frac{\pi}{2}\) undefined hai, is liye \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) kabhi value nahin; \(y = \frac{\pi}{2}\) horizontal asymptote hai.

book_ref.quote: Including \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) in the range

blocks.prompt:
28 Which interval does the principal \(\sec\) function use, and which does the principal \(\csc\) function use? What is removed from each?
(Principal \(\sec\) kaun sa interval istemal karta hai aur principal \(\csc\) kaun sa? Har aik se kya nikaala jata hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\sec\): cosine wala \([0, \pi]\), \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) nikaal kar; \(\csc\): sine wala \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\), \(0\) nikaal kar.

book_ref.quote: uses cosine's interval \([0, \pi]\)

blocks.prompt:
29 Define the principal cotangent function and give the domain and range of the inverse cotangent function.
(Principal cotangent function ki definition likhein aur inverse cotangent ki domain aur range batayein.)
blocks.explanation: Principal cotangent: \(\cot : (0, \pi) \to (-\infty, \infty)\) (bijective). \(y = \cot^{-1} x \iff x = \cot y\); domain \((-\infty, \infty)\), range \((0, \pi)\).

book_ref.quote: called principal cotangent function

blocks.prompt:
30 Find \(\cot^{-1} 1\) and \(\cot^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).
(\(\cot^{-1} 1\) aur \(\cot^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: So \(\cot^{-1} x\) is always strictly between 0 and \(\pi\)

blocks.prompt:
31 Find the value of \(\cos\left[\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]\).
(\(\cos\left[\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]\) ki qeemat nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Andar wala angle: \(-\frac{\pi}{6}\). Phir \(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: Method: work from the inside out.

blocks.prompt:
32 Find the value of \(\csc\left[\cot^{-1}(-1)\right]\).
(\(\csc\left[\cot^{-1}(-1)\right]\) ki qeemat nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: First find the inner angle

blocks.prompt:
33 Find the value of \(\sec\left[\cot^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right]\).
(\(\sec\left[\cot^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right]\) ki qeemat nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\cot^{-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\pi}{3}\), is liye \(\sec\frac{\pi}{3} = 2\).

book_ref.quote: Given: three expressions, each a trigonometric function of an inverse trigonometric value.

blocks.prompt:
34 Find the domain of \(f(x) = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3} - 1\right)\).
(\(f(x) = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3} - 1\right)\) ki domain nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(-1 \le \frac{x}{3} - 1 \le 1 \Rightarrow 0 \le x \le 6\). Domain: \([0, 6]\).

book_ref.quote: an inverse trigonometric function only accepts inputs from its own domain

blocks.prompt:
35 Find the domain of \(g(x) = \sin^{-1}(x^{2} - 3)\).
(\(g(x) = \sin^{-1}(x^{2} - 3)\) ki domain nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Andar wale expression ko [-1, 1] mein rakh kar dono shartein hal karein.

book_ref.quote: \(\cos^{-1}\) and \(\sin^{-1}\) need the input in \([-1, 1]\)

blocks.prompt:
36 Find the domain of \(h(x) = \csc^{-1}(x - 1)\).
(\(h(x) = \csc^{-1}(x - 1)\) ki domain nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(x - 1 \le -1\) ya \(x - 1 \ge 1\), yaani \(x \le 0\) ya \(x \ge 2\). Domain: \((-\infty, 0] \cup [2, \infty)\).

book_ref.quote: The table below summarizes the domains and ranges of the principal trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions.

blocks.prompt:
37 Find the domain of \(k(x) = \sec^{-1}\sqrt{x}\).
(\(k(x) = \sec^{-1}\sqrt{x}\) ki domain nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\sqrt{x}\) ke liye \(x \ge 0\); \(\sqrt{x}\) manfi nahin hota, is liye sirf \(\sqrt{x} \ge 1\): \(x \ge 1\). Domain: \([1, \infty)\).

book_ref.quote: remember any extra condition such as

blocks.prompt:
38 Find the domain of \(p(x) = \tan^{-1}(\ln x)\).
(\(p(x) = \tan^{-1}(\ln x)\) ki domain nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan^{-1}\) har real number leta hai; sirf \(\ln x\) ka mojood hona zaroori: \(x > 0\). Domain: \((0, \infty)\).

book_ref.quote: In domain questions, forgetting the domain of the inner function

blocks.prompt:
39 Is \(\cot^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = \tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\)? Explain.
(Kya \(\cot^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = \tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\)? Wazahat karein.)
blocks.explanation: Nahin. \(\cot^{-1}(-\sqrt{3}) = \frac{5\pi}{6}\), magar \(\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{6}\). Rishta \(\cot^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{x}\) sirf \(x > 0\) ke liye hai; yahan \(\frac{5\pi}{6} = \pi - \frac{\pi}{6}\).

book_ref.quote: Parts (i) and (ii) need no such restriction because the ranges already fit.

blocks.prompt:
40 If \(\tan^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{7}\), find \(\cot^{-1} x\).
(Agar \(\tan^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{7}\) ho to \(\cot^{-1} x\) nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan^{-1} x + \cot^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\), is liye \(\cot^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{7} = \frac{5\pi}{14}\).

book_ref.quote: each pair of 'co-functions' adds up to

blocks.prompt:
41 Solve \(\sin^{-1} x = \cos^{-1} x\).
(\(\sin^{-1} x = \cos^{-1} x\) ko hal karein.)

book_ref.quote: Hence proved: \(\sin^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\)

blocks.explanation: Angle ka naam rakhein, sin^2 + cos^2 = 1 se cosine nikalein, phir reciprocal lein.

book_ref.quote: 7, 24, 25 is a Pythagorean triple

steps: \(\sec\alpha = \frac{29}{21}\), aur \(\alpha\) \(\sec^{-1}\) ki range mein hai, is liye \(\alpha = \sec^{-1}\frac{29}{21}\)

blocks.prompt:
43 Without using a calculator, find \(\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{8}\right)\).
(Calculator ke baghair \(\cos\left(\frac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{8}\right)\) nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\cos\alpha = \frac{1}{8}\). \(\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{1 + \cos\alpha}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{9}{16}} = \frac{3}{4}\).

book_ref.quote: use the half-angle identity

blocks.text: 9.2 Sum and Difference Formulas for Inverse Trigonometric Functions

blocks.prompt:
44 State the sum and difference formulas for \(\tan^{-1}\), with the condition for each.
(\(\tan^{-1}\) ke jama aur tafreeq ke formulas un ki shart ke saath likhein.)

book_ref.quote: Give each inverse a name, \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\)

blocks.prompt:
45 Evaluate \(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{4} + \tan^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\).
(\(\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{4} + \tan^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\) ki qeemat nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Formula (v) needs \(1 - xy \ne 0\)

blocks.prompt:
46 Express \(\sin^{-1}\frac{4}{5} - \sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\) as a single inverse sine.
(\(\sin^{-1}\frac{4}{5} - \sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5}\) ko aik inverse sine ki shakal mein likhein.)

book_ref.quote: (ii) Same start as (i), but use

blocks.prompt:
47 Express \(2\tan^{-1}\frac{2}{3}\) as a single inverse tangent.
(\(2\tan^{-1}\frac{2}{3}\) ko aik inverse tangent ki shakal mein likhein.)

book_ref.quote: Further by putting \(y = x\) in (v), we get

blocks.prompt:
48 Show that \(2\tan^{-1} 2 \ne \tan^{-1}\frac{2 \cdot 2}{1 - 2^{2}}\). Which condition fails?
(Dikhayein ke \(2\tan^{-1} 2 \ne \tan^{-1}\frac{2 \cdot 2}{1 - 2^{2}}\). Kaun si shart toot-ti hai?)
blocks.explanation: \(\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)\) manfi hai magar \(2\tan^{-1} 2\) musbat (taqreeban \(2.214\)). Double formula ki shart \(-1 < x < 1\) hai; yahan \(x = 2\).

book_ref.quote: becomes \(x^{2} < 1\), that is \(-1 < x < 1\)

blocks.explanation: Bayen taraf formula (v) se jorein, hal karein, phir har root check karein.

book_ref.quote: so every root must be tested in the original equation

steps: Check: \(x = -1\) par bayen taraf manfi, \(\tan^{-1} 3\) musbat: radd. \(x = \frac{1}{2}\): \(\tan^{-1} 1 + \tan^{-1}\frac{1}{2} = \tan^{-1} 3\): sahi

blocks.prompt:
50 Use formula (iii) to evaluate \(\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{2} + \cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\), and check the answer.
(Formula (iii) se \(\cos^{-1}\frac{1}{2} + \cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\) nikalein aur jawab check karein.)

book_ref.quote: (iii) Let \(\cos^{-1}x = \alpha\), \(\cos^{-1}y = \beta\)

blocks.prompt:
51 With \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), show that \(\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} x \ne \sin^{-1}(2x)\).
(\(x = \frac{1}{2}\) le kar dikhayein ke \(\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} x \ne \sin^{-1}(2x)\).)
blocks.explanation: Bayen: \(\frac{\pi}{3}\). Dayen: \(\sin^{-1} 1 = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Barabar nahin; sahi: \(2\sin^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\left(2x\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}\).

book_ref.quote: Inverse functions do not add like that

blocks.prompt:
52 Verify \(\cos^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\) for \(x = \frac{3}{5}\), and show that it fails for \(x = -\frac{3}{5}\).
(\(x = \frac{3}{5}\) ke liye \(\cos^{-1} x = \sin^{-1}\sqrt{1 - x^{2}}\) ki tasdeeq karein, aur dikhayein ke \(x = -\frac{3}{5}\) par yeh ghalat hai.)
blocks.explanation: \(x = \frac{3}{5}\): \(\cos^{-1}\frac{3}{5} = \sin^{-1}\frac{4}{5}\). \(x = -\frac{3}{5}\): \(\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right) = \pi - \sin^{-1}\frac{4}{5}\) (obtuse), jab ke \(\sin^{-1}\frac{4}{5}\) acute. Yeh sirf \(0 \le x \le 1\) ke liye hai.

book_ref.quote: The same triangle idea turns any inverse function into another.
